title: HomePedia
description: Real estate market analysis platform ingesting 822K+ French property transactions, with geospatial queries, NLP sentiment analysis on city reviews, and 12-month price historic.
long_description:
HomePedia is a full-stack real estate intelligence platform built for the French market. It aggregates millions of records from open public datasets — DVF property transactions, DPE energy diagnostics, INSEE demographics, ANIL rental surveys, OpenStreetMap POIs, and citizen reviews scraped from bien-dans-ma-ville.fr.

The processing pipeline runs locally on PySpark and scales to Databricks Serverless in production, producing 26 aggregate tables and 15 GeoJSON cache layers stored across PostgreSQL 16 + PostGIS (relational & geospatial) and MongoDB 7 (sentiment documents). A multilingual BERT model scores city sentiment from thousands of user reviews, while a Prophet time-series model generates 12-month price forecasts per commune.

The Next.js frontend renders interactive Mapbox choropleth and bubble maps, letting users drill down from national region to individual commune with live filters for price, affordability, DPE rating, and sentiment score. Production deployment targets Kubernetes on AWS with Docker Compose for local development.

title: KubeQuest
description: Production Kubernetes cluster on AWS with GitOps via ArgoCD, zero-downtime rolling deployments, complete Prometheus/Grafana/Loki observability stack, and automated nightly backups.
long_description:
KubeQuest is a production-grade cloud infrastructure project demonstrating the full DevOps lifecycle for a containerized Laravel application.

The cluster runs on 4 AWS EC2 t4g.medium (ARM64 Graviton) instances in eu-west-3: a control plane with Elastic IP, two worker nodes, and a dedicated monitoring node. Traffic enters through an nginx-ingress controller with automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS via cert-manager.

GitOps is handled by ArgoCD using the "App of Apps" pattern — every infrastructure change goes through Git, giving a complete audit trail and one-command rollback. GitHub Actions builds Docker images on every commit, pushes them to GHCR, and updates the Helm values file; ArgoCD picks up the change and executes a zero-downtime rolling update (maxUnavailable: 0).

The observability stack (kube-prometheus-stack) runs on its own node: Prometheus scrapes metrics from kubelet, node-exporter, and kube-state-metrics; Grafana visualizes dashboards; Loki + Promtail centralise all pod logs. OPA Gatekeeper enforces admission control policies. Nightly CronJobs dump MySQL to MinIO (S3-compatible), and Velero backs up all Kubernetes manifests for full disaster recovery.

title: Visiobook
description: AI platform that transforms any text — novel, PDF, manuscript — into an animated VisioBook, orchestrating LLM semantic analysis, FLUX image generation, and LTX-Video animation across 10+ independent microservices.
long_description:
Visiobook is a production AI platform (Epitech ESP project) that turns written content into watchable animated video — think a graphic novel that comes to life. A user uploads a PDF, DOCX, or scanned document; the platform extracts the text, runs it through an LLM analysis pipeline to extract characters, scenes, narrative arcs, and sentiment; then generates bespoke illustrations for each scene and animates them into a final video VisioBook.

The backend is split across 10+ independent microservices communicating over NATS JetStream: a NestJS/TypeScript project orchestrator manages the multi-step workflow; a FastAPI AI analysis service runs Mistral Ministral-3B via vLLM for semantic extraction; a FastAPI media generation service drives ComfyUI on GPU (RunPod) to produce character reference images (FLUX.1-dev), scene illustrations (FLUX Redux for visual consistency), and animations (LTX-Video 2.3 22B two-pass with Gemma 3 prompt enhancement). A content ingestion service handles OCR (Tesseract), PDF parsing, and intelligent text chunking. The infrastructure runs on Kubernetes with Helm + Istio, with GPU inference accessed over Tailscale VPN.

Users interact through a native Flutter mobile app (iOS + Android) with a glassmorphism design system and 795 unit/widget tests, or through the web portal. Subscriptions and quotas are managed via Stripe. The platform is live in production at visiobook.cloud.

title: CriptoViz
description: Real-time crypto analytics dashboard with WebSocket price streaming from Binance, TimescaleDB time-series storage, multi-timeframe candlestick charts, and bilingual NLP sentiment analysis on live crypto news.
long_description:
CriptoViz is a microservices analytics platform for cryptocurrency markets. Four independent Python services run behind RabbitMQ: a scraper ingests data from Binance WebSockets, CoinGecko, and NewsAPI; an analytics service computes OHLCV aggregates and technical indicators (SMA 20/50/200, EMA 12/26, RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, ATR); a WebSocket delivery service fans out real-time updates to clients; and a sentiment service scores news headlines with a hybrid French/English NLP pipeline (custom lexicon + VADER fallback with automatic language detection).

Data lands in TimescaleDB with continuous aggregates across 7 timeframes (1 min to 1 week) for BTC, ETH, SOL, ADA, and DOT. The React 19 + TypeScript frontend renders live candlestick charts via Recharts, a live news feed with sentiment badges, and multi-indicator overlays — all updating in real time without page refresh. The full stack spins up with a single docker-compose command.

title: Travel Order Disorder
description: Multilingual NLP pipeline that extracts origin/destination cities from natural language travel requests and computes optimal rail routes via a Neo4j graph database — with optional voice input.
long_description:
Travel Order Disorder is an end-to-end NLP system that understands travel requests written (or spoken) in French or English, extracts the relevant city entities, and returns optimal railway itineraries.

The NLP layer uses a fine-tuned DistilBERT multilingual model for Named Entity Recognition, backed by CamemBERT for French-specific cases and spaCy as a lightweight fallback. The orchestrator handles three input modes: interactive CLI, CSV batch processing, and optional voice input via OpenAI Whisper.

Extracted entities are passed to an Express.js API that queries a Neo4j graph database containing railway station nodes and route edges. The graph returns complete itineraries with distance, duration, and intermediate stops. Results are exported as JSON or CSV with confidence scores and rejection reasons for invalid requests.

Everything runs in Docker Compose — the Neo4j instance, the TypeScript API, and the Python NLP service — making the full stack reproducible with a single command.

title: Zoidberg — Pneumonia Detection
description: Deep learning pipeline that automatically detects and classifies pneumonia from chest X-rays, benchmarking DenseNet-121, VGG16, ResNet50, and EfficientNetB0 with Grad-CAM explainability.
long_description:
Zoidberg is a medical imaging project focused on automated pneumonia detection from chest radiographs, distinguishing between bacterial and viral pneumonia using transfer learning on pre-trained CNNs.

The pipeline starts with thorough EDA and preprocessing — standardising image dimensions, applying an 80/10/10 train/val/test split, and handling the significant class imbalance through targeted augmentation strategies (rotations, flips, brightness jitter). Four architectures are trained and compared in parallel: DenseNet-121, VGG16, ResNet50 (including a multiclass variant), and EfficientNetB0.

EfficientNetB0 includes Grad-CAM activation map visualisation, producing heatmaps that highlight the X-ray regions most influential to the prediction — critical for clinical interpretability and trust. A detailed French-language technical report documents methodology, hyperparameter choices, and comparative results across all models and dataset variants.

title: TimeManager
description: Full-stack time tracking app with a REST API built in Elixir/Phoenix, a Vue.js SPA, JWT authentication, and a monitoring pipeline powered by Prometheus and Logstash.
long_description:
TimeManager is a production-oriented time management application. It demonstrates clean separation between a high-performance API layer and a reactive frontend, all orchestrated with Docker Compose.

The backend is an Elixir/Phoenix REST API handling users, clocks (session start/end), and working-hour aggregates, with JWT-based authentication securing all endpoints. The Vue.js frontend provides a responsive SPA for employees and managers to log work sessions, view history, and track time.

Infrastructure is managed via Docker Compose with separate dev and production configurations. Nginx acts as a reverse proxy routing API and frontend traffic. A Logstash pipeline processes and ships application logs, while Prometheus scrapes metrics for operational visibility — giving the project a production-ready observability footprint beyond a typical student app.

title: WINO
description: Two-sided marketplace connecting wine enthusiasts with wine shops offering curated tasting experiences — built with Ruby on Rails and deployed live on Heroku.
long_description:
WINO is a marketplace that pairs wine lovers seeking discovery with wine shops offering curated tasting sessions. The platform handles the full booking flow: shops list experiences with dates and capacity; explorers browse, filter, and book; both sides manage their profiles and history through a clean Rails MVC interface.

Built during Le Wagon's intensive bootcamp, the project demonstrates full-stack product development from domain modelling and database design through to SCSS styling, Stimulus JS interactivity, and cloud deployment. The live Heroku instance serves real traffic and includes Cloudinary image hosting for shop and experience photos.

WINO goes well beyond a tutorial app — covering authentication, role-based authorisation, file uploads, mailers, and a polished responsive UI.

title: Slowwave
description: Photography portfolio web application with dynamic galleries and minimalist design, built with Ruby on Rails.
long_description:
Slowwave is a personal photography portfolio. It serves as a showcase for photographic work across travel, street, and documentary genres.

Built on Ruby on Rails, the application includes a curated gallery system, SCSS-driven minimalist design with careful typographic choices, and modern frontend tooling.

The project pushed toward production quality with a Heroku deployment configuration, image optimisation, and a clean URL structure, more about craft and presentation than feature breadth.

title: CreativeHub
description: Two-sided marketplace connecting designers with freelance opportunities and companies seeking design proposals — built with Ruby on Rails.
long_description:
CreativeHub is a Le Wagon bootcamp project built as a team during an intensive development sprint. The platform bridges two audiences: designers looking for their next freelance gig, and companies that need design proposals for advertising and branding campaigns.

The application follows a classic two-sided marketplace pattern — companies post briefs with requirements and budget; designers browse, apply, and submit proposals; both sides manage their activity through dedicated dashboards. Built on Ruby on Rails with the Le Wagon rails-templates production stack, it features Devise authentication, Cloudinary image uploads, real time chat and a responsive SCSS-designed interface.

CreativeHub, is a fully-shipped product rather than a prototype — something the team built end-to-end in a matter of weeks.

title: Trinity Food Market
description: Full-stack food market management platform with a Node.js/Express API, Vue.js SPA, Docker Compose orchestration for dev and production profiles, and native Android support via Capacitor.
long_description:
Trinity Food Market is a cross-platform food marketplace application built with a clean separation between backend and frontend, both containerised and wired together through Docker Compose.

The backend exposes a REST API built on Node.js, handling inventory, orders, and user management. The Vue.js frontend provides the customer-facing SPA with product browsing and ordering flows. A data population script lets the team seed the database from JSON files — useful for development and demo environments. The project ships with two Docker Compose profiles: dev (with hot-reload) and prod (optimised, production-ready).

A standout feature is native Android support via Capacitor, which wraps the Vue.js web app into a native Android binary — giving the project a true cross-platform reach from a single codebase.

title: EventScraper
description: Made as a job technical chanllenge, EventScraper is an event aggregation platform that scrapes Eventbrite, TripAdvisor, and Facebook to centralise activities in one place, with an interactive map and Google Dialogflow AI assistant for natural language queries.
long_description:
EventScraper solves a real friction point: events are scattered across Eventbrite, TripAdvisor, and Facebook, forcing users to check three platforms. This app aggregates them all into a single, searchable feed with an interactive OpenStreetMap overlay showing event locations.

The backend is a Python/Flask service that drives the scrapers and exposes a REST API. The Vue.js + Vuetify frontend provides a clean, responsive UI with filtering by category, date, and location. The standout feature is a Google Dialogflow-powered AI assistant that lets users query events in natural language ("What's happening near me this weekend?") — the intent is parsed and translated into API filters.

The project also lays groundwork for future expansion: GetYourGuide, Funbooker, and Civitatis integrations are planned, along with user authentication and a unified date-format layer across scraped sources.

title: AFP Content Manager
description: Internal content management tool developed as a job technical chanllenge for to streamline editorial workflow and content operations.
long_description: AFP Content Manager is an internal tool built as a demo for Agence France-Presse, the French international news wire service. The project supports editorial and content operations workflows within the AFP ecosystem.

title: ArenaMatrix CSV Uploader
description: Rails web app that ingests reservation CSV exports from ArenaMatrix and presents them as a searchable, filterable table — with Docker packaging and Render deployment.
long_description:
ArenaMatrix CSV Uploader is a focused utility built to bridge ArenaMatrix reservation data with a clean web interface. Users upload CSV exports from the ArenaMatrix system; the Rails app parses, stores, and displays the records in a searchable, sortable table.

The project is intentionally scoped — it solves one problem well rather than trying to be a full-featured CRM. The Rails MVC structure keeps the parsing and display logic clean. A Dockerfile and render.yaml configuration make deployment straightforward on Render's platform.
